RECOMMENDED ALL-SHARE COMBINATION
of
80 MILE PLC
by
GREENLAND ENERGY COMPANY
to be effected by means of a scheme of arrangement under Part 26 of the Companies Act 2006
Summary

The boards of Greenland Energy Company (“Greenland Energy”) and 80 Mile plc (“80 Mile”) are pleased to announce that they have reached agreement on the terms of a recommended all-share combination of Greenland Energy with 80 Mile (the “Combination”). It is intended that the Combination will be implemented by way of a Court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement under Part 26 of the Companies Act (“Scheme”).
Under the terms of the Combination, 80 Mile Shareholders will be entitled to receive:
for each 80 Mile Share 0.0079485 New Greenland Energy Stock (the “Exchange Ratio”)

On 11 November, being the close of business on the last day prior to the date of this Announcement, the terms of the Combination value each 80 Mile Share at 1.28 pence per share based on the closing Greenland Energy share price of $2.14 and £/US$ exchange rate of US$1.33 : £1.00 (the “Offer Value”).
The Offer Value implies 80 Mile’s entire issued and to be issued share capital is valued at approximately £74 million on a fully diluted basis.

Upon completion of the Combination, 80 Mile Shareholders will own approximately 50 per cent. of the Combined Company and Greenland Energy Stockholders will own approximately 50 per cent. of the Combined Company.
The Offer Value represents a premium of approximately:
71 per cent. to the Closing Price per 80 Mile Share of 0.75 pence on 7 September 2026 (being the last Business Day prior to the date the Offer Period commenced); and
28 per cent. to the Closing Price per 80 Mile Share of 1.00 pence on 11 November 2026 (being the last practicable date prior to the date of this Announcement).

In order to allot the New Greenland Energy Stock, Greenland Energy will be required to seek the approval of the Greenland Energy Stockholders at the Greenland Energy Stockholder Meeting. The Combination is accordingly conditional on such approval being obtained. It is expected that the Greenland Energy Proxy Statement, which will contain notice of the Greenland Energy Stockholder Meeting will be published and sent to the Greenland Energy Stockholders at or around the same time as the Scheme Document is posted to 80 Mile Shareholders.

The terms of the possible Combination were originally announced on 8 September 2026 with an exchange ratio which valued each 80 Mile Share at 1.1 pence per share based on the closing Greenland Energy share price of $1.37 and £/US$ exchange rate of US$1.35 : £1.00 on 4 September 2026, being the close of business on the last trading day on Nasdaq prior to the announcement by 80 Mile of a possible offer by Greenland Energy. This exchange ratio was originally proposed in conjunction with a proposed warrant issuance by Greenland Energy to the Greenland Energy Stockholders. Following further discussions between Greenland Energy and 80 Mile, Greenland Energy no longer intends to issue warrants to existing Greenland Energy Stockholders and as a consequence 80 Mile Shareholders will not suffer the dilutive impact of this proposal. The Exchange Ratio was accordingly amended in part to reflect this as set out above, as announced by 80 Mile on 3 November 2026.

The Exchange Ratio assumes that 160,500,000 new 80 Mile Shares are issued, comprising shares issued to participants in the 80 Mile Share Schemes and 5,000,000 80 Mile Shares issued to SP Angel pursuant to the exercise of its warrants, as these have an exercise price lower than the implied current value per 80 Mile Share of the Exchange Ratio.

The Exchange Ratio assumes that no 80 Mile Shareholder will receive any dividend, distribution, or other return of value from 80 Mile prior to the Scheme becoming Effective. If 80 Mile announces, declares or pays any dividend (or any dividend becomes payable) or makes any other distribution or return of value or capital to its shareholders after the date of this Announcement and on or prior to the Effective Date, Greenland Energy reserves the right to make an equivalent reduction to the consideration offered to the 80 Mile Shareholders by way of a reduction in the Exchange Ratio at the Relevant Exchange Rate in which case any reference in this Announcement or in the Scheme Document to the consideration payable under the terms of the Combination will be deemed to be a reference to the consideration as so reduced. In such circumstances, 80 Mile Shareholders shall be entitled to retain any such dividend, distribution, or other return of value declared, made, or paid.

It is intended that the Combination will be implemented by way of a court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement under Part 26 of the Companies Act (although Greenland Energy reserves the right to effect the Combination by way of an Offer, subject to the consent of the Panel and the terms of the Co-operation Agreement). The Conditions to the Combination (including the Material Regulatory Conditions highlighted in paragraph 7) are set out in full in Appendix I to this Announcement.
Recommendation of the Independent 80 Mile Directors

The Independent 80 Mile Directors, who have been so advised by SP Angel as to the financial terms of the Combination, consider the terms of the Combination to be fair and reasonable. SP Angel is providing independent financial advice to the Independent 80 Mile Directors for the purposes of Rule 3 of the Code. In providing its advice to the Independent 80 Mile Directors, SP Angel has taken into account the commercial assessments of the Independent 80 Mile Directors.

Accordingly, the Independent 80 Mile Directors intend to recommend unanimously that 80 Mile Shareholders vote in favour of the Scheme at the Court Meeting and the resolutions relating to the Combination at the 80 Mile General Meeting (and if Greenland Energy, with the consent of the Panel and subject to the terms of the Co-operation Agreement, subsequently structures the Combination as an Offer, to accept any Offer by Greenland Energy), as the Independent 80 Mile Directors who hold 80 Mile Shares have irrevocably undertaken to do in respect of their own beneficial holdings, being, in aggregate, 38,037,811 80 Mile Shares, representing approximately 0.68 per cent. of the existing issued ordinary share capital of 80 Mile as at 11 November 2026 (being the last practicable date prior to this Announcement).

In addition, an irrevocable undertaking to vote in favour of the Scheme (and if Greenland Energy, subject to the consent of the Panel and the terms of the Co-operation Agreement, subsequently structures the Combination as an Offer, to accept any Offer by Greenland Energy) has been received from Roderick McIllree in respect of an aggregate of 622,662,514 80 Mile Shares representing approximately 11.12 per cent. of the existing issued ordinary share capital of 80 Mile as at 11 November 2026 (being the last practicable date prior to the date of this Announcement).

The Greenland Energy Directors have unanimously approved the Combination and intend to recommend unanimously that Greenland Energy Stockholders vote in favour of the issuance of the New Greenland Energy Stock in connection with the Combination, as the Greenland Energy Directors who hold Greenland Energy Stock have irrevocably undertaken to do in respect of their own beneficial holdings, being, in aggregate, 9,456,428 Greenland Energy Stock, representing approximately 21.58 per cent. of the existing issued ordinary share capital of Greenland Energy as at 11 November 2026 (being the last practicable date prior to this Announcement). Canaccord Genuity has acted as financial adviser in the UK to the Greenland Energy Directors in relation to the Combination.
Strategic Rationale
The Greenland Energy Board and the 80 Mile Board believe there is a compelling strategic rationale for the Combination for the following reasons:

Greenland Energy and 80 Mile are existing joint venture partners in the Jameson Land Basin project in Greenland. The proposed merger would consolidate 100% ownership of those licences in a single Nasdaq-listed vehicle and also bring together 80 Mile’s remaining portfolio with Greenland Energy’s capital markets access and development capability, creating a diversified energy and critical minerals company.

80 Mile’s operations require sustained capital investment before they become financially self-sustaining and reach their full potential. Greenland Energy brings a significantly stronger financial position, including USD 37.4 million in cash and cash equivalents as of 30 June 2026, a stronger shareholder register and access to lower-cost financing and more funding, likely enabling the combined entity to fund working capital, business development, and growth projects on materially better terms than 80 Mile could achieve on a standalone basis. This financial strength ensures that 80 Mile’s high-quality assets are less constrained by capital availability, volatility in equity capital markets, and can be advanced at the pace the geology and market opportunity deserve.

The Combination is expected to streamline each company’s operating footprint by reducing duplicative corporate functions, consolidating overlapping regional infrastructure, and by creating a single, more efficient operating model. By integrating 80 Mile’s assets into Greenland Energy’s existing operational framework, the combined group will benefit from simplified reporting lines, consolidated expertise, and a leaner corporate structure - allowing management to focus more resources on the assets themselves rather than the administrative complexity of managing a joint venture.
Background to and reasons for the Recommendation of the Independent 80 Mile Directors

The Independent 80 Mile Directors have considered the alternative strategic options available to 80 Mile and the likelihood of successfully executing them. These include remaining independent and funding its projects through further equity placings, further asset-level farm-outs or disposals, or a sale to a third party. The Independent 80 Mile Directors believe that material institutional funding on AIM for companies of 80 Mile's size and large-scale hydrocarbon projects is limited, and that further equity funding would be likely to be available only at a significant discount and would be materially dilutive to 80 Mile Shareholders. Asset-level transactions have already been put in place with Greenland Energy and USFM and are therefore not available to meet 80 Mile's corporate funding needs.

In considering the financial terms of the Combination and determining whether they reflect an appropriate valuation of 80 Mile and its future prospects, the Independent 80 Mile Directors took into account a range of factors, including:

Premium: a significant premium to 80 Mile’s volume-weighted average share price before the initial announcement was made, noting that the price and volume of 80 Mile Shares had been driven up by the acquisition of 80 Mile Shares by Greenland Energy immediately prior to the receipt of the non-binding indicative offer for the proposed Combination;

Financial Position and Funding: 80 Mile’s operations require sustained capital investment before they become financially self-sustaining and reach their full potential. Greenland Energy brings a significantly stronger financial position, including USD 37.4 million in cash and cash equivalents as of 30 June 2026, a stronger shareholder register and access to lower-cost financing and more funding, likely enabling the combined entity to fund working capital, business development, and growth projects on materially better terms than 80 Mile could achieve on a standalone basis. This financial strength ensures that 80 Mile’s high-quality assets are less constrained by capital availability, volatility in equity capital markets, and can be advanced at the pace the geology and market opportunity deserve. Greenland Energy's financial resources and access to US capital markets, where it raised approximately US$70 million in April 2026, would significantly reduce the funding risk for the next stage of exploration or development of the Jameson Land Basin, the Greenswitch biodiesel plant, and for 80 Mile's Disko-Nuussuaq and Dundas projects in Greenland. Greenland Energy also agreed to advance a £3 million convertible loan to fund 80 Mile’s articulated strategy in the coming months, on competitive terms. The Loan will provide 80 Mile with interim funding which is essential to protect business continuity and the value of 80 Mile for all 80 Mile Shareholders.

Consolidation of the Jameson Project: the Combination would bring the Jameson Land Basin licences, and the party responsible for funding and permitting the drilling programme, into a single group. 80 Mile Shareholders would gain exposure to the whole project, rather than a 30 per cent. carried interest whose value depends on Greenland Energy completing its earn-in;

Synergies and streamlining of operations: The Combination is expected to streamline each company's operating footprint by reducing duplicative corporate functions, consolidating overlapping regional infrastructure, and creating a single, more efficient operating model. By integrating 80 Mile's assets into Greenland Energy’s existing operational framework, the combined group will benefit from simplified reporting lines, consolidated expertise, and a leaner corporate structure - allowing management to focus more resources on the assets themselves rather than the administrative complexity of managing a joint venture.

Continued participation: as the consideration is entirely in Greenland Energy Stock, 80 Mile Shareholders would retain exposure to 80 Mile's projects, through a substantial shareholding in the enlarged group, and would share in its future value;
Scale and costs: the enlarged group would have greater scale and access to a wider investor base on Nasdaq, and duplicated listed-company costs would be removed; and
Government Funding: U.S.-incorporated and managed entities can more easily access government funding, which has significantly scaled up in the last couple of years.

In considering the recommendation of the Combination to 80 Mile Shareholders, the Independent 80 Mile Directors have given due consideration to Greenland Energy's intentions in respect of the 80 Mile Group’s management, employees, and stakeholders. In particular, the Independent 80 Mile Directors note that Greenland Energy has confirmed that it will seek to continue with the growth plan for the Greenswitch biodiesel business in Italy, the exploration and development of 80 Mile’s projects in Greenland and the importance placed by 80 Mile on the existing employees and other stakeholders of 80 Mile.

The Independent 80 Mile Directors believe that the Combination represents a positive outcome for 80 Mile Shareholders, 80 Mile’s employees and 80 Mile’s other stakeholders in Greenland and Italy, where the Combination could potentially lead to more employment opportunities and investment in the communities in which 80 Mile operates. Furthermore, the Independent 80 Mile Directors consider that the Combination has the potential to lead to more growth through an increased rate of exploration and development of the 80 Mile Group’s projects in Greenland and a faster pace of development of its biodiesel plant in Italy.

Accordingly, the Independent 80 Mile Directors believe that the terms of the Combination are in the best interests of 80 Mile Shareholders as a whole and unanimously recommend that 80 Mile Shareholders vote in favour of the resolutions to be proposed at the Court Meeting and the 80 Mile General Meeting (or, in the event that the Combination is implemented by way of a takeover offer, to accept or procure the acceptance of such offer).

The Independent 80 Mile Directors, who have been so advised by SP Angel (who are providing independent financial advice to the Independent 80 Mile Directors for the purposes of Rule 3 of the Takeover Code) as to the financial terms of the Combination, consider the terms of the Combination to be fair and reasonable. In providing its financial advice to the Independent 80 Mile Directors, SP Angel has taken into account the commercial assessments of the Independent 80 Mile Directors.
Background to and reasons for the Combination by Greenland Energy
Background

Greenland Energy Company's relationship with 80 Mile plc originated through March GL Company’s interests in the Jameson Land Basin in East Greenland (the “Jameson Project”). In September 2025, March GL Company (“March GL”), which at the time was not a member of the Greenland Energy Group, entered into a farm out agreement with 80 Mile, pursuant to which March GL obtained the right to earn up to a 70 per cent. working interest in the Jameson Project by funding the first two exploration wells (the “Farm Out Agreement”). This established a significant commercial relationship between March GL and 80 Mile, with March GL assuming substantial funding and development responsibilities and 80 Mile retaining an interest in the Jameson Project.

Following the completion of Greenland Energy's business combination in March 2026, March GL became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Greenland Energy. After its approximately US$70 million public offering in April 2026, Greenland Energy continued to advance preparations for its Jameson Project exploration programme. During this period, the parties discussed a proposed two-year extension of the existing farm out arrangements to provide additional flexibility for the development of the Jameson Project. In the course of those discussions, 80 Mile suggested that Greenland Energy consider acquiring 80 Mile rather than proceeding solely with an extension of the existing arrangements.

Given the strategic importance of the Jameson Project to Greenland Energy, Larry Swets, Chairman of Greenland Energy, and Robert Price, its Chief Executive Officer, entered into preliminary discussions with representatives of 80 Mile regarding a potential combination. Those discussions considered the opportunity to consolidate the parties' respective interests in the Jameson Project, simplify their existing contractual relationship and combine 80 Mile's broader portfolio of natural resource assets with Greenland Energy's financial resources, development capabilities and access to the U.S. capital markets.

As discussions progressed, the parties explored an all-share combination under which Greenland Energy might acquire 80 Mile at an indicative value of 1.10 pence per 80 Mile Share, with the exchange ratio to be finalised.

In early September 2026, the Greenland Energy Board considered the Combination, including its strategic rationale, indicative economic terms, potential dilution to existing Greenland Energy Stockholders and the applicable U.S. and UK regulatory requirements. The Greenland Energy Board also considered the potential issuance to existing Greenland Energy Stockholders of warrants to acquire additional Greenland Energy Stock at an exercise price of US$1.50 per share, as a means of providing those shareholders with an opportunity to participate further in the Combined Company. The proposed warrant issuance remained subject to further consideration and finalisation of its terms. Roderick McIllree, who held positions and interests in both companies and was a director of Greenland Energy until 20 October 2026, recused himself from the Greenland Energy Board's and the 80 Mile Board’s respective deliberations concerning the Combination.

On 8 September 2026, Greenland Energy and 80 Mile announced that they had agreed indicative terms for a proposed all-share acquisition. Under those terms, 80 Mile Shareholders would receive approximately 0.01108 newly issued Greenland Energy Stock for each 80 Mile Share, representing an indicative value of approximately 1.10 pence per 80 Mile Share based on Greenland Energy's closing share price on 4 September 2026 and the exchange rate used in the announcement.

Following the announcement, the parties and their respective advisers continued confirmatory due diligence and work on the transaction documentation and applicable U.S. and UK, Greenlandic, Finnish and Italian regulatory requirements. In parallel, on 23 September 2026 the parties amended the existing Jameson Project arrangements with Greenland Energy assuming March GL's rights and obligations under the Farm Out Agreement, the drilling longstop dates being extended to 31 December 2028 and Greenland Energy assuming responsibility for obtaining and maintaining the required drilling permits and approvals.

The terms of the possible Combination that were originally announced on 8 September 2026 were proposed in conjunction with a proposed warrant issuance by Greenland Energy to the Greenland Energy Stockholders. Following further discussions between Greenland Energy and 80 Mile, Greenland Energy no longer intends to issue warrants to existing Greenland Energy Stockholders and as a consequence 80 Mile Shareholders will not suffer the dilutive impact of this proposal. The Exchange Ratio was accordingly amended to 0.0079485 newly issued Greenland Energy Stock for each 80 Mile Share, representing an indicative value of approximately 1.596 pence per 80 Mile Share based on Greenland Energy's closing share price on 2 November 2026 and the exchange rate used in that announcement. The amendment to the proposed exchange ratio was made in part to reflect the removal of the proposed Greenland Energy warrants, as announced by 80 Mile on 3 November 2026.

Greenland Energy and 80 Mile have agreed the terms of an unsecured convertible loan of £3 million with a tenure of 12 months. 80 Mile’s current cash resources are not expected to be sufficient to execute its articulated strategy, including in particular, the ramp-up of the 80 Mile Group’s Italian biodiesel operations, through to completion of the Combination, which could take several months. The terms of the Loan are summarised at paragraph 13 of this Announcement.
The Combination is subject to the Conditions and further terms set out in this Announcement and to be set out in the Scheme Document.
Reasons for the Combination

In considering the Combination, the Greenland Energy Board evaluated the strategic benefits of combining the two companies in light of their existing commercial relationship, the importance of the Jameson Project to Greenland Energy's long term strategy and the opportunity to create a larger and more diversified natural resources company with a particular focus on Greenland.
Consolidation of the Jameson Project interests

A principal consideration was the opportunity to consolidate the parties' respective interests in the Jameson Project within a single corporate group. Under the existing Farm Out Agreement, Greenland Energy has the right to earn up to a 70 per cent. working interest by funding the first two exploration wells, with 80 Mile retaining the remaining interest. The Combination would bring those interests under common ownership, align economic ownership more closely with Greenland Energy's funding and development responsibilities and simplify the existing contractual and governance arrangements. It would also provide greater strategic and operational alignment in relation to the future development of the Jameson Project.
Greater scale and a broader asset base

The Greenland Energy Board also considered the opportunity to broaden Greenland Energy's asset portfolio through the addition of 80 Mile's other natural resource interests, including Disko-Nuussuaq and Dundas in Greenland and its interests in Finland and Italy. The Combination would create greater scale and breadth across the Combined Company, with a broader portfolio of natural resource assets. This would provide greater flexibility to assess development priorities, allocate capital across the portfolio and pursue strategic partnerships, potential asset monetisations and future development opportunities.
Complementary resources and capabilities

Greenland Energy's financial resources, development capabilities and access to the U.S. capital markets would be combined with 80 Mile's portfolio, technical and operational experience and established presence in Greenland. The Combined Company would also benefit from the respective technical, operational and capital markets experience of the two organisations, providing a broader platform from which to advance the combined portfolio and pursue longer term investment and development opportunities, particularly in Greenland.
More efficient corporate and operational structure

The proposed combination would provide an opportunity to streamline the existing corporate and operational arrangements, reduce duplication and coordinate capital allocation across the enlarged portfolio. The extent of any efficiencies would depend on the successful integration of the businesses and subsequent management decisions.
Preservation of financial resources and continuing participation

The all-share consideration was a further factor. It would allow Greenland Energy to preserve cash for its exploration programme and other corporate requirements, while providing 80 Mile Shareholders with an ongoing equity interest in the Combined Company and continued exposure to the combined portfolio.

Taken together, these considerations supported the Greenland Energy Board's decision to pursue the Combination as an evolution of Greenland Energy's existing relationship with 80 Mile and an opportunity to establish a larger, more diversified natural resources company with a particular focus on Greenland.
Irrevocable Undertakings

Greenland Energy has received irrevocable undertakings to vote in favour of the Scheme at the Court Meeting and the resolutions relating to the Combination at the 80 Mile General Meeting from the Independent 80 Mile Directors, in respect of their entire beneficial holdings, amounting to 38,037,811 80 Mile Shares, in aggregate, representing approximately 0.68 per cent. of the issued share capital of 80 Mile as at 11 November 2026, being the last practicable date prior to this Announcement.

Greenland Energy has also received irrevocable undertakings to vote in favour of the Scheme at the Court Meeting and the resolutions relating to the Combination at the 80 Mile General Meeting from Roderick McIllree, in respect of his entire beneficial holdings, amounting to 622,662,514 80 Mile Shares, in aggregate, representing approximately 11.12 per cent. of the issued share capital of 80 Mile as at 11 November 2026, being the last practicable date prior to this Announcement.

Greenland Energy has also received irrevocable undertakings from the Greenland Energy Directors who hold Greenland Energy Stock to vote in favour of all resolutions at the Greenland Energy Stockholder Meeting in respect of, in aggregate, 9,456,428 Greenland Energy Stock, representing approximately 21.58 per cent. of the voting rights of the Greenland Energy Stock in issue as at 11 November, being the last practicable date prior to the date of this Announcement.
Further details of these irrevocable undertakings are set out in Appendix III.
Combination details and timetable
It is intended that the Combination will be implemented by way of a Court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement under Part 26 of the Companies Act (or, if Greenland Energy so elects, an Offer).
The Combination will be on the terms and subject to the Conditions set out in Appendix I to this Announcement and to be set out in the Scheme Document. The Conditions include, amongst others:

the approval by a majority in number of Scheme Shareholders who are present and voting (and entitled to vote) at the Scheme Voting Record Time, whether in person or by proxy, at the Court Meeting, and who represent not less than 75 per cent. in value of the Scheme Shares;
the passing of all resolutions required to approve and implement the Scheme by the requisite majority or majorities of the 80 Mile Shareholders at the 80 Mile General Meeting;

the satisfaction or waiver of the Material Regulatory Conditions further detailed in paragraph 7 of this Announcement, to which the attention of shareholders is specifically drawn, and should be read carefully;
no member of the Wider 80 Mile Group taking steps or having steps taken against them for their winding-up or the commencement of any other insolvency related process;

the issuance of the New Greenland Energy Stock in connection with the Combination being duly approved by the affirmative vote of the majority of the votes cast, in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote on the matter, at the Greenland Energy Stockholder Meeting;
confirmation having been received by Greenland Energy that the New Greenland Energy Stock has been approved for listing, subject to official notice of issuance, on Nasdaq;
the sanction of the Scheme by the Court with or without modification (but subject to any such modification being acceptable to Greenland Energy and 80 Mile); and
following the sanction of the Scheme by the Court, the delivery of a copy of the Court Order to the Registrar of Companies for registration.

The Combination is expected to become Effective in the first half of 2027, subject to the satisfaction (or, where applicable, waiver) of the Conditions set out in Appendix I to this Announcement. An expected timetable of principal events will be included in the Scheme Document.

It is expected that the Scheme Document, containing further information about the Combination and notices of the Court Meeting and the 80 Mile General Meeting, will be posted to 80 Mile Shareholders (other than those resident in Restricted Jurisdictions) along with the Forms of Proxy on 10 December 2026. The timing of publication will also take into account the timing of the filing of the Greenland Energy Proxy Statement in accordance with SEC rules and any potential review of the preliminary proxy statement by the SEC. In the event that this results in a delay to the anticipated publication of the Scheme Document, 80 Mile and Greenland Energy may approach the Panel to request an extension to the 28 day period required under paragraph 3(a) of Appendix 7 of the Code, with a view to enabling the shareholder materials to be published to 80 Mile Shareholders on or around the same date as the Greenland Energy Proxy Statement is posted to Greenland Energy Stockholders.

Subject to certain restrictions relating to persons resident in Restricted Jurisdictions, the Scheme Document will also be made available on Greenland Energy’s website at https://greenlandenergyco.com/offering/ and 80 Mile’s website at https://www.80mile.com/offer-microsite, and the Greenland Energy Proxy Statement will also be made available on Greenland Energy’s website at https://greenlandenergyco.com/investor-relations/ by following the link to “All SEC Filings” button.
Commenting on the Combination, Robert Price, Chief Executive Officer of Greenland Energy, said:

“This combination builds on our existing partnership and brings our respective Jameson Land interests under common ownership. It would simplify the development structure, preserve cash through an all share transaction and provide greater flexibility to prioritise investment across the combined portfolio.”
Commenting on the Combination, Mike Hutchinson, Chairman of 80 Mile, said:

“Greenland Energy has a significantly stronger financial position and a stronger shareholder register, which we expect to let the combined company fund working capital, business development and growth projects on materially better terms than 80 Mile could achieve on its own, so that high-quality assets can be advanced at the pace the geology and market opportunity deserve. Because the proposed transaction is structured as an all-share exchange, the Company’s shareholders are not being asked to give up their exposure to the existing business; holding around 50% of an enlarged U.S.-listed business. All of this comes as Greenland’s potential for natural resources meets growing demand and as the strengthening relationship between Greenland, Denmark and the United States supports responsible resource investment and investor confidence.”
Acquisition of 80 Mile Shares by Greenland Energy

Between and including 25 August 2026 and 3 September 2026 Greenland Energy purchased a total of 246,765,352 80 Mile Shares at prices between 0.53p and 0.82p per 80 Mile Share and the weighted average price was 0.73p per 80 Mile Share. During the same period the price of an 80 Mile Share increased from a closing mid-market price of 0.54p to 0.77p per 80 Mile Share. As at 8 September 2026 Greenland Energy is interested in 246,765,352 80 Mile Shares representing 4.41% of 80 Mile’s existing issued share capital.

As a consequence of these dealings under Rule 6.1(a) of the Code any offer by Greenland Energy for 80 Mile, save with the consent of the Panel, must be on no less favourable terms than the highest price paid in the 3 months prior to the commencement of the Offer Period, being 0.82p.

Strategic Rationale
The Greenland Energy Board and the 80 Mile Board believe there is a compelling strategic rationale for the Combination for the following reasons:

Greenland Energy and 80 Mile are existing joint venture partners in the Jameson Land Basin project in Greenland. The proposed merger would consolidate 100% ownership of those licences in a single Nasdaq-listed vehicle and also bring together 80 Mile‘s remaining portfolio with Greenland Energy’s capital markets access and development capability, creating a diversified energy and critical minerals company.

80 Mile’s operations require sustained capital investment before they become financially self-sustaining and reach their full potential. Greenland Energy brings a significantly stronger financial position, including USD 37.4 million in cash and cash equivalents as of 30 June 2026, a stronger shareholder register and access to lower-cost financing and more funding, likely enabling the combined entity to fund working capital, business development, and growth projects on materially better terms than 80 Mile could achieve on a standalone basis. This financial strength ensures that 80 Mile’s high-quality assets are less constrained by capital availability, volatility in equity capital markets, and can be advanced at the pace the geology and market opportunity deserve.

The Combination is expected to streamline each company’s operating footprint by reducing duplicative corporate functions, consolidating overlapping regional infrastructure, and by creating a single, more efficient operating model. By integrating 80 Mile’s assets into Greenland Energy’s existing operational framework, the combined group will benefit from simplified reporting lines, consolidated expertise, and a leaner corporate structure - allowing management to focus more resources on the assets themselves rather than the administrative complexity of managing a joint venture.
Background to and reasons for the Recommendation of the Independent 80 Mile Directors

The Independent 80 Mile Directors have considered the alternative strategic options available to 80 Mile and the likelihood of successfully executing them. These include remaining independent and funding its projects through further equity placings, further asset-level farm-outs or disposals, or a sale to a third party. The Independent 80 Mile Directors believe that material institutional funding on AIM for companies of 80 Mile's size and large-scale hydrocarbon projects is limited, and that further equity funding would be likely to be available only at a significant discount and would be materially dilutive to 80 Mile Shareholders. Asset-level transactions have already been put in place with Greenland Energy and USFM and are therefore not available to meet 80 Mile's corporate funding needs.

In considering the financial terms of the Combination and determining whether they reflect an appropriate valuation of 80 Mile and its future prospects, the Independent 80 Mile Directors took into account a range of factors, including:

Premium: a significant premium to 80 Mile’s volume-weighted average share price before the initial announcement was made, noting that the price and volume of 80 Mile Shares had been driven up by the acquisition of 80 Mile Shares by Greenland Energy immediately prior to the receipt of the non-binding indicative offer being made for the proposed Combination;

Financial Position and Funding: 80 Mile’s operations require sustained capital investment before they become financially self-sustaining and reach their full potential. Greenland Energy brings a significantly stronger financial position, including USD 37.4 million in cash and cash equivalents as of 30 June 2026, a stronger shareholder register and access to lower-cost financing and more funding, likely enabling the combined entity to fund working capital, business development, and growth projects on materially better terms than 80 Mile could achieve on a standalone basis. This financial strength ensures that 80 Mile’s high-quality assets are less constrained by capital availability, volatility in equity capital markets, and can be advanced at the pace the geology and market opportunity deserve. Greenland Energy's financial resources and access to US capital markets, where it raised approximately US$70 million in April 2026, would significantly reduce the funding risk for the next stage of exploration or development of the Jameson Land Basin, the Greenswitch biodiesel plant, and for 80 Mile's Disko-Nuussuaq and Dundas projects in Greenland. Greenland Energy also agreed to advance a £3 million convertible loan to fund 80 Mile’s articulated strategy in the coming months, on competitive terms. The Loan will provide 80 Mile with interim funding which is necessary to protect business continuity and the value of 80 Mile for all 80 Mile Shareholders.

Consolidation of the Jameson Project: the Combination would bring the Jameson Land Basin licences, and the party responsible for funding and permitting the drilling programme, into a single group. 80 Mile Shareholders would gain exposure to the whole project, rather than a 30 per cent. carried interest whose value depends on Greenland Energy completing its earn-in;

Synergies and streamlining of operations: The Combination is expected to streamline each company's operating footprint by reducing duplicative corporate functions, consolidating overlapping regional infrastructure, and creating a single, more efficient operating model. By integrating 80 Mile's assets into Greenland Energy’s existing operational framework, the combined group will benefit from simplified reporting lines, consolidated expertise, and a leaner corporate structure — allowing management to focus more resources on the assets themselves rather than the administrative complexity of managing a joint venture.

Continued participation: as the consideration is entirely in Greenland Energy Stock, 80 Mile Shareholders would retain exposure to 80 Mile's projects, through a substantial shareholding in the enlarged group, and would share in its future value;
Scale and costs: the enlarged group would have greater scale and access to a wider investor base on Nasdaq, and duplicated listed-company costs would be removed; and
Government Funding: U.S.-incorporated and managed entities can more easily access government funding, which has significantly scaled up in the last couple of years.

In considering the recommendation of the Combination to 80 Mile Shareholders, the Independent 80 Mile Directors have given due consideration to Greenland Energy's intentions in respect of the 80 Mile Group’s management, employees, and stakeholders. Background to and reasons for the Combination by Greenland Energy
Background

Greenland Energy’s relationship with 80 Mile originated through March GL Company’s interests in the Jameson Land Basin in East Greenland (the “Jameson Project”). In September 2025, March GL Company (“March GL”), which at the time was not a member of the Greenland Energy Group, entered into a farm out agreement with 80 Mile, pursuant to which March GL obtained the right to earn up to a 70 per cent. working interest in the Jameson Project by funding the first two exploration wells (the “Farm Out Agreement”). This established a significant commercial relationship between March GL and 80 Mile, with March GL assuming substantial funding and development responsibilities and 80 Mile retaining an interest in the Jameson Project.

Following the completion of Greenland Energy's business combination in March 2026, March GL became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Greenland Energy. After its approximately US$70 million public offering in April 2026, Greenland Energy continued to advance preparations for its Jameson Project exploration programme. During this period, the parties discussed a proposed two-year extension of the existing farm out arrangements to provide additional flexibility for the development of the Jameson Project. In the course of those discussions, 80 Mile suggested that Greenland Energy consider acquiring 80 Mile rather than proceeding solely with an extension of the existing arrangements.

Given the strategic importance of the Jameson Project to Greenland Energy, Larry Swets, Chairman of Greenland Energy, and Robert Price, its Chief Executive Officer, entered into preliminary discussions with representatives of 80 Mile regarding a potential combination. Those discussions considered the opportunity to consolidate the parties' respective interests in the Jameson Project, simplify their existing contractual relationship and combine 80 Mile's broader portfolio of natural resource assets with Greenland Energy's financial resources, development capabilities and access to the U.S. capital markets.

As discussions progressed, the parties explored an all-share combination under which Greenland Energy might acquire 80 Mile at an indicative value of 1.10 pence per 80 Mile Share, with the exchange ratio to be finalised.

In early September 2026, the Greenland Energy Board considered the Combination, including its strategic rationale, indicative economic terms, potential dilution to existing Greenland Energy Stockholders and the applicable U.S. and UK regulatory requirements. The Greenland Energy Board also considered the potential issuance to existing Greenland Energy Stockholders of warrants to acquire additional Greenland Energy Stock at an exercise price of US$1.50 per share, as a means of providing those shareholders with an opportunity to participate further in the Combined Company. The proposed warrant issuance remained subject to further consideration and finalisation of its terms. Roderick McIllree, who held positions and interests in both companies and was a director of Greenland Energy until 20 October 2026, recused himself from the Greenland Energy Board's and the 80 Mile Board’s respective deliberations concerning the Combination.

On 8 September 2026, Greenland Energy and 80 Mile announced that they had agreed indicative terms for a proposed all-share acquisition. Under those terms, 80 Mile Shareholders would receive approximately 0.01108 newly issued Greenland Energy Stock for each 80 Mile Share, representing an indicative value of approximately 1.10 pence per 80 Mile Share based on Greenland Energy's closing share price on 4 September 2026 and the exchange rate used in the announcement.

Following the announcement, the parties and their respective advisers continued confirmatory due diligence and work on the transaction documentation and applicable U.S. and UK, Greenlandic, Finnish and Italian regulatory requirements. In parallel, on 23 September 2026 the parties amended the existing Jameson Project arrangements with Greenland Energy assuming March GL's rights and obligations under the Farm Out Agreement, the drilling longstop dates being extended to 31 December 2028 and Greenland Energy assuming responsibility for obtaining and maintaining the required drilling permits and approvals.

The terms of the possible Combination that were originally announced on 8 September 2026 were proposed in conjunction with a proposed warrant issuance by Greenland Energy to the Greenland Energy Stockholders. Following further discussions between Greenland Energy and 80 Mile, Greenland Energy no longer intends to issue warrants to existing Greenland Energy Stockholders and as a consequence 80 Mile Shareholders will not suffer the dilutive impact of this proposal. The Exchange Ratio was accordingly amended to 0.0079485 newly issued Greenland Energy Stock for each 80 Mile Share, representing an indicative value of approximately 1.596 pence per 80 Mile Share based on Greenland Energy's closing share price on 2 November 2026 and the exchange rate used in that announcement. The amendment to the proposed exchange ratio was made in part to reflect the removal of the proposed Greenland Energy warrants, as announced by 80 Mile on 3 November 2026.

Greenland Energy and 80 Mile have agreed the terms of an unsecured convertible loan of £3 million with a tenure of 12 months. 80 Mile’s current cash resources are not expected to be sufficient to execute its articulated strategy, including in particular, the ramp-up of the 80 Mile Group’s Italian biodiesel operations, through to completion of the Combination, which could take several months. The terms of the Loan are summarised at paragraph 13 of this Announcement.
The Combination is subject to the Conditions and further terms set out in this Announcement and to be set out in the Scheme Document.
Reasons for the Combination

In considering the Combination, the Greenland Energy Board evaluated the strategic benefits of combining the two companies in light of their existing commercial relationship, the importance of the Jameson Project to Greenland Energy's long term strategy and the opportunity to create a larger and more diversified natural resources company with a particular focus on Greenland.
Consolidation of the Jameson Project interests

A principal consideration was the opportunity to consolidate the parties' respective interests in the Jameson Project within a single corporate group. Under the existing Farm Out Agreement, Greenland Energy has the right to earn up to a 70 per cent. working interest by funding the first two exploration wells, with 80 Mile retaining the remaining interest. The Combination would bring those interests under common ownership, align economic ownership more closely with Greenland Energy's funding and development responsibilities and simplify the existing contractual and governance arrangements. It would also provide greater strategic and operational alignment in relation to the future development of the Jameson Project.
Greater scale and a broader asset base

The Greenland Energy Board also considered the opportunity to broaden Greenland Energy's asset portfolio through the addition of 80 Mile's other natural resource interests, including Disko-Nuussuaq and Dundas in Greenland and its interests in Finland and Italy. The Combination would create greater scale and breadth across the Combined Company, with a broader portfolio of natural resource assets. This would provide greater flexibility to assess development priorities, allocate capital across the portfolio and pursue strategic partnerships, potential asset monetisations and future development opportunities.
Complementary resources and capabilities

Greenland Energy's financial resources, development capabilities and access to the U.S. capital markets would be combined with 80 Mile's portfolio, technical and operational experience and established presence in Greenland. The Combined Company would also benefit from the respective technical, operational and capital markets experience of the two organisations, providing a broader platform from which to advance the combined portfolio and pursue longer term investment and development opportunities, particularly in Greenland.
More efficient corporate and operational structure

The proposed combination would provide an opportunity to streamline the existing corporate and operational arrangements, reduce duplication and coordinate capital allocation across the enlarged portfolio. The extent of any efficiencies would depend on the successful integration of the businesses and subsequent management decisions.
Preservation of financial resources and continuing participation

The all-share consideration was a further factor. It would allow Greenland Energy to preserve cash for its exploration programme and other corporate requirements, while providing 80 Mile Shareholders with an ongoing equity interest in the Combined Company and continued exposure to the combined portfolio.

Taken together, these considerations supported the Greenland Energy Board's decision to pursue the Combination as an evolution of Greenland Energy's existing relationship with 80 Mile and an opportunity to establish a larger, more diversified natural resources company with a particular focus on Greenland.
